title: Use distinct terms for deciding part and workers across firstmate page
summary: Newcomers to the firstmate study page see one word, 'agent', for both firstmate's deciding part and the workers. Pick two terms and apply them to the glossary, intro, every card in model.json, the rendered rationales and findings text, and site.rs. State on the page which term 'decided by' means. Also address the other seven rating findings, which this retry's earlier attempt mostly handled.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the newcomer-visible wording and a repo sweep for the retired term, not just that files changed.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check must pass, with site tests updated.
A test asserts rendered card text contains no ambiguous 'agent'.
Single focused wording and renderer change on one study page.
Wording is written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: newcomers reading the published firstmate study page, and the verifier who checks it.
Terms chosen: 'judge' (or similar) for the deciding part and 'worker' for task-running agents; the word 'agent' is dropped or kept only where unambiguous and listed with a reason.
Claim texts in claims.json (18 uses of 'agent') are out of scope and unchanged; if a claim quote is rendered on cards, the card wording around it must make the sense clear.
The earlier attempt's other fixes (captain/yolo defined, home entry, t10 explanation, ra1-ra6 titles, reopened relabel, study-id) are redone from base, since changes were discarded.
The t10 summary cites c12 and c13 for the t4 teardown claim, as the verifier's nit asked.
The 'decided by' label may be a data-model value (evaluated_by 'agent'); renderer maps it to the new term so tests' fixture values still work.

acceptance_criteria.text: The glossary defines two distinct terms, one for firstmate's deciding part and one for the task-running workers, and the page says which term 'decided by' refers to.

Every use of 'agent' in model.json cards (triggers, failure, changes text such as t8 'no agent is running' and 'the running agent is replaced'), in rationales.json, findings.json and intro.json is replaced with the matching term, or is unambiguous and listed with a reason in the job notes.
The text generated by xtask/src/site.rs (evaluated-by labels such as 'decided by ...') uses the new term and no longer prints 'decided by agent' or 'checked by agent'.
The job includes the output of a search for 'agent' across studies/firstmate-work-handling/*.json (except claims.json) and xtask/src/site.rs, with each remaining hit justified.
In 'Start here', 'captain' and 'yolo' are defined in plain words at or before first use; the glossary has a 'home' entry.
The t10 yolo-merge card explains why it is ready → ready while t4 leads to done, citing c12/c13 as well as c26-c29.

Cards ra1-ra6 each have a short topic title beside the id; the reopened state no longer shows a bare 'terminal-success' tag and says it stays open waiting for the captain; the lede explains or drops the raw study id. Opening paragraphs and Next steps keep their wording.

Run `cargo test`: site tests pass, including a new assertion that rendered card, rationale and findings text from the real study contains no ambiguous 'agent', and every cited claim id resolves. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Changing the opening paragraphs or the Next steps section
Adding a new generic pre-verification checking tool to Athena itself
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference: many files and a repo-wide terminology sweep, plus redoing all seven rating fixes from base.
